Thought: I need to determine what happens when alcohols/polyols react with anhydrides. This is a chemical reaction question.

When alcohols (R-OH) or polyols (compounds with multiple -OH groups) react with anhydrides (typically acid anhydrides like acetic anhydride), they undergo an esterification reaction. 

The general reaction is:
R-OH + (R'-CO)₂O → R'-COOR + R'-COOH

In this reaction:
- The alcohol (R-OH) reacts with the anhydride ((R'-CO)₂O)
- This produces an ester (R'-COOR)
- And also produces a carboxylic acid (R'-COOH)

So the products of this reaction are an ester and a carboxylic acid (which is an acid).

Looking at the options:
A. Acids and esters are formed - This matches the products of the reaction
B. Bases are formed - No bases are formed in this reaction
C. Salt is formed - No salts are formed in this reaction
D. Water is formed - Water is not a product of this reaction
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
